value.source_content: The undergraduate program in Computer Science aims to develop students’ breadth of knowledge across the subject areas of computer science, including their ability to apply the defining processes of computer science theory, abstraction, design, and implementation to solve problems in the discipline. Students take a set of core courses. After learning the essential programming techniques and the mathematical foundations of computer science, students take courses in programming techniques, automata and complexity theory, systems programming, computer architecture, analysis of algorithms, artificial intelligence, and applications. The program prepares students for careers in government, law, and the corporate sector and for graduate study.

value.source_content: Declaring the major is a straightforward process, and there are no specific course or major requirements you need to complete beforehand. Please note that processing can take up to two weeks, and we’re unable to expedite requests. We encourage students to plan ahead, especially if you have a target date for declaring. Additionally, keep in mind that we do not process declarations during finals week, academic breaks, or the Summer quarter. To get started, please follow the how to declare steps outlined on the CS website.

value.source_content: Guide to Choosing Introductory Courses Students arriving at Stanford have widely differing backgrounds and goals, but most find that using computers effectively benefits their education. The department offers many introductory courses to meet the needs of these students. For students whose principal interest is exposure to the fundamental ideas behind computer science and programming, course or course are the most appropriate courses. They are intended for students in nontechnical disciplines who expect to make some use of computers but do not expect to go on to more advanced courses. course and course meet the Ways of Thinking Ways of Doing breadth requirements in Formal Reasoning and include an introduction to programming and the use of modern Internet-based technologies. Students interested in computer use should consider course , Introduction to Computing at Stanford. Students who intend to pursue a serious course of study in computer science may enter the program at various levels, depending on their background. Students with little prior experience or those who wish to take more time to study the fundamentals of programming should take course , followed by course . Students in course need not have prior programming experience. Students with significant previous exposure to programming or those who want an intensive introduction to the field may start directly in course . course uses Python as its programming language; course uses C++. No prior knowledge of these languages is assumed, and the previous programming experience required for course may be in any language. In all cases, students are encouraged to discuss their background with the instructors responsible for these courses. After the introductory sequence, Computer Science majors and those needing a significant computer science background for related engineering majors should take course , course , and course or course . course offers an introduction to the mathematical and theoretical foundations of computer science. course exposes students to various programming concepts that illustrate critical strategies used in systems development; course and course build on this material, focusing on the development of larger-scale software, using systems and networking abstractions. In summary: For Exposure: CS1C : Introduction to Computing at Stanford For nontechnical use: CS101: Introduction to Computing Principles OR CS105: Introduction to Computers For scientific use and a technical introduction: CS106A: Programming Methodology For significant use: CS106A: Programming Methodology & course : Programming Abstractions CS103: Mathematical Foundations of Computing CS107: Computer Organization and Systems course : Principles of Computer Systems OR CS111: Operating Systems Principles Overseas Studies Courses in Computer Science See the listings in ExploreCourses or the Bing Overseas Studies website for course descriptions and additional offerings. Students should consult their department or program’s student services office for the applicability of Overseas Studies courses to a major or minor program. See the Handbook for Undergraduate Engineering Programs (UGHB) for additional information and sample programs,

facts.value: ACT or SAT is required for first-year applicants. Stanford has no minimum score and no score guarantees admission. Either exam is accepted without preference; the redesigned ACT and original ACT are accepted, and the redesigned ACT science section is optional. Applicants self-report highest scores; official scores are required for self-reported scores if admitted and enrolling. SAT is superscored across highest Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Math sections; ACT superscore may be reported with highest section scores. Writing/essay portions are optional. Stanford recommends tests within five years.

The current Stanford page accepts both original and redesigned ACT versions and states the redesigned ACT science section is optional. It does not name a single SAT form/edition cutoff; SAT section superscoring is described. No exemption from the ACT-or-SAT requirement is published on the reviewed current first-year testing page.

Required components include Common Application; school report and counselor recommendation; official high-school transcript/academic results (grades 9–12); and two academic-teacher recommendations. School officials/testing agencies must send official records directly; applicant-submitted transcripts are not accepted. Report international curriculum results and predictions when available. Any high-school, college/university, or online courses absent from the current high-school transcript require official records.

Besides the Common App personal essay, applicants answer several Stanford short questions (each up to 50 words) and write three Stanford short essays, each 100–250 words: an idea/experience that excites learning; a note to a future roommate; and a distinctive contribution based on life experiences, interests, and character.

For 2027 entry, REA Common Application deadline is November 1, with decisions by mid-December; RD deadline is January 5, with decisions by early April. Submit by 11:59 p.m. in the applicant's local timezone. REA is nonbinding. If admitted, reply by May 1. Application with Optional Arts Portfolio uses earlier application deadlines: October 15 REA and December 5 RD.

First-year applicants who attend high school in an interview area and apply REA or RD may be invited to an optional alumni interview. Availability depends on interview-area coverage and volunteer availability; applicants cannot request or schedule one. Not receiving an interview is not a disadvantage.

Optional arts portfolios are available in Art Practice, Dance, Music, and Theater and Performance Studies for applicants wishing to show exceptional fine/performing-arts achievement. Portfolio submission does not require an arts major. Submission is through Stanford's portal after the Common Application; areas have specific materials. Music and Theater/Performance Studies may include an optional arts recommendation; none accepted for Art Practice or Dance. Mail-in items are not returned.

Undergraduate international applicants are reviewed in the context of the educational system, country, and school resources where they attend secondary school. The application process otherwise follows the same first-year or transfer route regardless of citizenship/residence. Undergraduate English-proficiency exams are not required; fluency in English is an admission prerequisite, and applicants may self-report English exam scores if they wish.

Stanford says it meets demonstrated need for admitted undergraduates regardless of citizenship when aid was requested during the application process. For international citizens, requesting aid is a factor in admission evaluation and makes the process more selective; an international citizen who applies without aid and enrolls after admission is generally ineligible to request undergraduate aid later. US citizens/permanent residents studying abroad remain domestic for aid evaluation.

Anyone who earned college credit in an associate or bachelor's degree program after high-school completion must use the transfer route. High-school/college dual-enrollment students apply as first-year. Transfer credit must be from an accredited degree-granting institution; vocational, technical, performance, or professional-program credit is excluded. Applicants need a high-school diploma/equivalent/GED to enroll. Applicants with an earned bachelor's degree are not eligible for undergraduate admission.

Stanford permits at most 90 quarter units of transfer credit (approximately two full-time years). Transfer entrants must complete at least two years of full-time enrollment at Stanford to earn a bachelor's degree, regardless of prior coursework.

Official Stanford transfer pages conflict: the general Transfer Applicants requirements page lists USD 90; the dedicated Application Fee/Fee Waiver page says USD 100. Both describe a nonrefundable fee and Common App fee-waiver request. Do not display a single confirmed amount until Stanford resolves the discrepancy.

Required materials: Common Application; fee or fee-waiver request; official high-school transcript including graduation date (or equivalent); official transcript from every college/university attended; College Report completed by an official at current/most recent institution; and two academic-instructor recommendations. International leaving exams (A-levels, IB, national exams) must be sent directly by school/testing agency; any AP results taken must all be self-reported. Official school materials are arranged through the school official. A midyear college transcript is not required.

Transfer applicants submit a personal statement about reasons for transferring and objectives (250–650 words), several short responses (50-word limit), and Stanford short essays including a learning-excitement response (100–250 words), one choice between a roommate note or community definition/contribution essay (100–250 words), and a distinctive contribution response. Prospective major/career interests are nonbinding.

Transfer Common Application deadline is March 15 at 11:59 p.m. applicant local time. Missing-document notice is in April, decisions are released by mid-May, and admitted applicants reply by June 2. All new transfer entrants begin in autumn/fall; no winter or spring start is offered. The official page does not label a calendar year for this recurring deadline.

Transfer applicants may submit a reviewed optional portfolio in Art Practice, Dance, Music, or Theater and Performance Studies; portfolio submission does not require majoring in the arts. Application is due March 15 and materials March 20 through the Stanford portal. Music and Theater/Performance Studies may include optional arts recommendation letters; Art Practice and Dance do not accept these letters. Mailed items are not returned.

facts.value: Published standard undergraduate budget for 2026–27 academic year (Autumn, Winter, Spring; typical full-time student): tuition USD 67,731; housing and food 22,944; student-fees allowance 2,610; books/supplies allowance 855; personal expenses allowance 3,405; travel varies; total USD 97,545. New first-year and transfer students also have one-time orientation USD 525 and document USD 250 fees included in their budget. Tuition, fees, housing, and food are billed quarterly; books, supplies, personal and travel amounts are planning allowances, generally not billed. Health insurance is required; Cardinal Care is assumed in budget for international students, while many other undergraduates waive it with other adequate coverage.

Stanford describes undergraduate aid as need-based and says it meets demonstrated need for admitted applicants, including international citizens, who request aid during admission. It does not offer merit scholarships except a limited number of athletic scholarships. Domestic admission is need-blind; need can be considered for some international applicants. Estimate with the official net price calculator; aid is not a guaranteed reduction until assessed and awarded.

Priority filing dates and expected notification on Stanford's central new-student/continuing-student aid page: first-year REA November 15, aid notification mid-December; first-year RD February 15, notification early April; transfer March 15, notification mid-May; continuing student April 30, notification in August. These are aid application deadlines, separate from admission deadlines. The page does not state a specific entering academic year for the new-student priority-date table.

Financial aid is reassessed for continuing undergraduates each academic year rather than being a fixed four-year amount. For 2026–27, continuing US citizen/eligible noncitizen aid priority date is April 30 with CSS Profile/IDOC and FAFSA; institutional scholarship consideration requires CSS, FAFSA, and tax documents. Continuing international applicants file CSS Profile and required student tax documents by April 30; published award notification date is June 15. Students requesting scholarship beyond four years/twelve quarters must submit a Request for Extended Aid Eligibility.

facts.value: For transfer entrants in the published 2026–27 aid checklist, US citizens/eligible noncitizens submit CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC (parent tax records); priority date March 15 and mid-May aid notification. CSS Profile, FAFSA and tax documents are all required for institutional scholarship; CSS is not required if seeking only federal/state aid. International transfer applicants use CSS Profile and International Student Supplement; Canadian citizens submit specified Canadian tax records through IDOC and do not submit the supplement. Applicants unable to pay CSS fee or in a country where payment is unavailable may use ISAFA. Divorced/separated/never-married parents submit separate CSS profiles; noncustodial-parent waiver requires supporting documents. International applicants must request aid in the admission application.

Published undergraduate aid types include need-based Stanford University Scholarship (CSS Profile-based; no separate application for individual scholarship funds), federal Pell and Supplemental Educational Opportunity grants (FAFSA-based, automatic consideration), student employment including Federal Work-Study/community-service work study, outside scholarships, and federal Direct/PLUS loans. Stanford says loans are not expected to meet ordinary college costs but may be requested. Stanford does not currently participate in California Student Aid Programs; institutional funds replace Cal Grant for most otherwise-eligible students, with rare stated exceptions. Need-based international aid is from institutional funds; international request affects admission review and aid is limited. A small number of athletic scholarships are the stated merit-aid exception.

Matriculated frosh are guaranteed 12 complete or partial academic-year housing quarters; transfer students receive nine. Housing eligibility requires enrollment and application by the first housing deadline and participation in later rounds when needed. If a guarantee-space assignment is unavailable, guaranteed students are housed by the end of the first week, potentially in temporary guest rooms or graduate residences. Enrolled first-year students are required to live in a university-designated residence unless an exception is announced.

Stanford undergraduate residences include live-in faculty or senior-staff Resident Fellows and trained residential staff; Residential Education programming is described as academic, social, and personal support. New frosh and transfer housing assignments are handled by R&DE Student Housing and are associated with the required first-year residence policy.

Stanford University is in Stanford, California, in the San Francisco Bay Area; Stanford's official postal location is Stanford, CA 94305, United States. Campus location and residential campus context do not determine applicant residency/fee classification.

facts.value: All new Stanford students, including frosh, undergraduate transfers, and graduate students, must complete entry health requirements: immunization records, screening, and when indicated testing/forms. Current public page lists August 15, 2026 for Autumn 2026 entrants and marks Autumn 2027 date not yet published; winter/spring 2027 dates are TBD. Requirements differ for standard nonmedical versus medical/PA students. Medical or religious exemption requests must be filed by the published deadline for the entry quarter. Vaden's 2026 guidance says nonmedical students require MMR documentation and TB screening, with other vaccines recommended or risk-specific; medical/PA requirements are more extensive.

Stanford's published 2026–27 first-year aid checklists distinguish Restrictive Early Action from Regular Decision and domestic/eligible-noncitizen/undocumented from international applicants. For US citizens and eligible noncitizens, CSS Profile (school code 4704), FAFSA (001305), and IDOC parent 2024 federal tax returns/forms are due Nov 15 for REA (mid-December notice) or Feb 15 for RD (April notice). If parents are divorced, separated or never married, each completes a CSS Profile and both submit tax documents; FAFSA parent is the parent providing more support. A noncustodial-parent waiver requires signed request and supporting documentation through IDOC. CSS Profile, FAFSA and IDOC are needed for institutional scholarship; CSS is not required if seeking only federal/state aid. Undocumented students follow domestic dates and submit CSS Profile/tax documents but do not file FAFSA. International aid applicants must request aid on the admission application and submit CSS Profile plus the International Student Supplement; Canadian citizens submit 2024 Canadian tax statements through IDOC and do not submit the supplement. If an international applicant cannot pay the CSS fee or College Board payments are unavailable in their country, the current checklist permits ISAFA instead. For international REA, priority date is Nov 15/mid-December notification; RD is Feb 15/April notification. Divorced/separated/never-married parents each complete CSS; a noncustodial-parent waiver requires evidence through Document Upload.

REA applicants cannot also apply to a private US university under EA, REA, ED or Early Notification, or to a public university under binding early admission. Other RD applications are allowed; after Stanford denial or deferral, EDII elsewhere is allowed. Concurrent exceptions include nonbinding public early admission, nonbinding rolling admission, nonbinding non-US admission, military academies, and nonbinding early submission required for scholarship or special-program consideration. MIT EA is explicitly excluded. Deferred applicants send the provided update form rather than reapply.

facts.value: AA pages state MS TOEFL 90 / IELTS 7 and PhD TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7. Those TOEFL cutoffs use the prior scale while Stanford has introduced a new TOEFL score scale for tests from Jan 21, 2026. The department page also lists exemptions for US citizen/permanent resident, English first language, English-taught postsecondary degree, or two consecutive years of English-medium experience in the last 10 years.

Full-time Aero/Astro MS has one Autumn 2027-28 cycle with a final December 1, 2026 deadline. A bachelor’s degree and strong technical preparation in engineering, physics, or comparable science are expected; the specific major is not fixed. Submit the online application, USD 125 fee, two-page single-spaced purpose statement, three recommendations (one academic required; two preferred), scanned transcripts, and English score if applicable. No late applications.

GRE is not required and not considered. The department says MS students are typically self-funded; assistantships may be possible and outside fellowships/loans are potential options. Federal student loans require U.S. citizenship or permanent residence. The AA part-time working-professional MS cannot be completed entirely online; some campus coursework is required and the route best suits locally employed students.

Aero/Astro PhD has one final Autumn 2027-28 deadline: December 1, 2026. Applicants may apply with a bachelor’s degree; a prior MS is not required. Current Stanford AA MS students who want to add a PhD must finish department paperwork before conferring the MS. PhD entrants without a related MS must add the AA MS internally by petition and approved program proposal at/before beginning year three.

PhD application requires online form, USD 125 fee, two-page single-spaced research purpose statement, three references (one academic required, two preferred), transcripts, and English test if applicable. Students in good standing receive support through thesis submission, at least equivalent to a 20-hour RA salary plus tuition for required enrollment; support sources include fellowship, RA, training grants or TA, with Cardinal Care insurance described by the department.

The nonrefundable non-professional graduate application fee is USD 125, due at submission. Eligible applicants may request GRE fee-reduction, program-participation, or school-based waivers before applying; submit at least 10 business days before the program deadline for timely review.

Standard application requires three academic or professional references, a statement of purpose, experience information and program-tailored supplemental responses. CV/resume, writing samples and other materials vary by program.

CEE maintains merit-based financial aid through teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and/or fellowships. Applicants interested in merit-based aid are asked to indicate that interest in the graduate application.

Chemical Engineering does not require GRE scores and will not accept them; it publishes no minimum GPA and no required prior field of study or other graduate degree. The department does not accept recommendation letters through Interfolio.

Engineering coterm applicants must be current Stanford undergraduates with a declared major,120 units toward graduation (including applicable AP/transfer units), and six non-summer Stanford quarters by intended entry; undergraduate transfer entrants need only two non-summer Stanford quarters. At least one quarter must overlap active undergraduate and graduate careers. Admission/acceptance must precede bachelor conferral. Department deadlines and criteria vary.

CS coterm is only for current, registered Stanford undergraduates and requires at least 120 units toward graduation; students on leave are ineligible. Apply no later than the quarter before expected BS completion. Submit Registrar forms, statement of purpose, resume, unofficial transcripts and three recommendation letters; at least two academic and one CS-faculty recommender are recommended. There is no minimum GPA; 3.5 is recommended for non-CS majors, who are also advised to complete four CS core courses or a mix of core/graduate courses. CS limits applicants to three coterm attempts. The 2026-27/2027-28 deadlines are Winter Oct 6 2026, Spring Jan 8 2027, Autumn Apr 30 2027. A USD 125 fee is assessed only if admitted and accepting. No deferral is allowed; late letters can miss committee review and submitted applications cannot be edited.

CS MS applicants need a qualifying bachelor’s degree but need not major in CS; the department recommends strong quantitative/analytical preparation and directs applicants to review its CS Foundation requirements. The MS can be coursework-only or include research. HCP is a part-time MS route for full-time employed people; HCP applicants must reside in the U.S., and international HCP applicants must be employed and located in the U.S. A CS MS is not a guaranteed path to the CS PhD.

CS says GRE is not required and is not considered for MS applicants. Its FAQ says TOEFL is required for applicants whose first language is not English regardless of citizenship, with stated exceptions for U.S. citizens/permanent residents, English first language, or an English-instruction degree. The central Graduate Admissions page also recognizes two years of consecutive full-time English-medium professional/educational experience as an exemption; CS MS FAQ does not mention that exemption.

Applicants need a qualifying bachelor’s degree; a CS major is not required, but strong quantitative and analytical skills are important. The PhD is research-oriented, with few course requirements and typical completion in 5–6 years. CS does not require or consider GRE scores. The SOP limit is 8,000 characters including spaces; three references and application checklist items are required. Applicants must choose CS MS or PhD and cannot apply to both in the same admissions cycle.

CS states all PhD students are guaranteed funding while they make satisfactory academic progress. External support must be disclosed and may adjust Stanford’s award. A 50% research assistantship covers 8–10 units of tuition and pays salary; lower 10–40% appointments or other funding combinations provide less tuition allowance/salary. RA availability depends on a faculty member, and students must be registered, in good standing, and satisfy payroll requirements.

EE MS is a terminal coursework-based program with 45 units, no thesis, and a typical full-time completion time of 1.5–2 years. It has autumn entry only; deadline for Autumn 2027-28 is Dec 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific and offer response is due Apr 15, 2027. Later PhD study requires applying through the separate PhD process.

EE PhD has autumn-only admission; Autumn 2027-28 deadline is Dec 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific, with decisions in late February and offer response due Apr 15, 2027. An MS is not required; typical completion is 5–7 years. Students in good standing receive full support for the PhD duration: year-one fellowship, usually advisor RA thereafter, full-time tuition, living stipend/salary and 50% Cardinal Care premium subsidy. Conditions include advisor/funding arrangement, 8–10 units during academic quarters, GPA at least 3.0 and timely progress. External tuition-plus-stipend awards typically replace the first fellowship.

EE does not require GRE. The department requests unofficial transcripts from every attended college, a purpose statement up to two single-spaced pages, three recommendations, and a USD 125 application fee. TOEFL/IELTS is required unless a central Graduate Admissions waiver applies; EE gives TOEFL 90 / IELTS 7 for admission consideration and TOEFL 109 / IELTS 8 to avoid the placement test. Applicants may request both the SoE and department application fee waivers, but only one is granted; EE preference is low-income or first-generation U.S. citizens/permanent residents.

School of Engineering departments award graduate fellowships, research assistantships, and teaching assistantships. The Bulletin does not establish a schoolwide funding amount, guarantee, eligibility, or deadline.

For 2027-28 entry, if no exemption applies, official TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic is required. Minimum consideration scores: TOEFL 90 before Jan 21 2026 or 4.5 on/after that date; IELTS Academic 7. Score validity is two years. Individual programs may require higher scores.

Environmental Social Sciences PhD admits for fall only. For the 2027-28 cycle, the application deadline is November 17, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific; applicants must choose the Environmental Behavioral Sciences (EBS) or Global Environmental Policy (GEP) subplan, and late applications are not accepted.

Geophysics admits to the department rather than an individual advisor or research group. The committee weighs academic achievement, recommendations, statement of purpose, research fit and potential, and work/life experience holistically; it states no minimum GPA. Applicants are encouraged to contact faculty about research fit and upcoming advising capacity. Applicants pursuing the Geophysics MS as a first step toward a PhD are asked to contact potential faculty advisors; applicants with a BS or MS may apply to the PhD.
Applicants may apply to one Stanford graduate degree program per academic year; the sole stated exception is applying to two Biosciences PhD programs in one application.

For non-professional graduate admission, applicants must hold or expect before enrollment a U.S. bachelor's degree or recognized international equivalent. Citizens and residents of all countries are eligible; a department may impose additional preparation and selection rules.

GRE General and Subject test requirements are set program by program as required, optional, or not considered. For 2027-28, the university's earliest valid test date is Sept 1 2021; a program may use a stricter period.

CEE accepts fall graduate applications once annually through Stanford Graduate Admissions. Required materials are uploaded academic records from every college/university attended for at least a year or current degree enrollment, statement of purpose (maximum three single-spaced pages, two recommended), three recommendations, resume/CV, and TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic if no exemption applies. Official transcripts are requested only after an admitted applicant accepts. GRE is not considered; Interfolio recommendations and emailed materials are not accepted. Applicants with related non-CEE backgrounds may apply but may need extra preparatory study after admission.

For Autumn 2027 entry, CEE MS, Engineer and PhD applications and supporting materials are due December 1, 2026 at 11:59 pm Pacific Standard Time; the same date applies to coterm MS. Fee waiver requests should be made by November 17, 2026, ten business days before the deadline. Decisions are released February-April 2027; admitted applicants must reply by April 15, 2027. Admitted MS students can request a one-time deferral to the next autumn by June 30, 2027; PhD and Engineer admits cannot use this deferral.

CEE FAQ still states old-scale TOEFL 90 for School of Engineering MS applicants, while central Graduate Admissions publishes the revised TOEFL scale for tests on/after January 21, 2026. The current application page defers to central TOEFL iBT/IELTS Academic rules and exemptions. Do not apply the FAQ score to a new-scale 2027 applicant without resolution.

CEE MS is a coursework-based degree with core courses, technical electives, seminars and unrestricted electives; thesis and research are not required. It can be finished in three quarters, though most students take four or five. CEE aims to support MS students where possible, usually describing any award in the admission letter. RA positions for MS are rare and usually in the second study year; course assistantships are competitive and generally favor continuing students. Neither is guaranteed.

CEE PhD combines coursework and research, requires service as teaching assistant for one course, and averages five to six years. Engineering PhD students in good standing receive support through thesis submission at least equivalent to a 20-hour RA salary plus tuition for required enrollment and Cardinal Care insurance. Support may come from fellowship, RA, training grant or TA; the department/advisor arranges it and cannot require external funding or self-funding as a condition of entry or continuation. Entering PhD applicants are considered for Engineering/Doerr fellowships with the admission application; Stanford Graduate Fellowships are selectively nominated and offer 12 quarters of stipend plus tuition for 8-10 units.

CEE Engineer degree is a post-master's professional research route requiring a thesis and approximately one to two further full-time years after the MS. The current external graduate directory explicitly lists CEE Engineer alongside MS/PhD for Autumn 2027 admission, with December 1, 2026 deadline and GRE not considered. CEE says any MS/Engineer support would generally appear in the admission letter; no guaranteed Engineer award or renewal schedule is published on the reviewed funding page.

MS&E MS applicants need an engineering or related quantitative degree with multivariable differential calculus and linear algebra. The department expects both this mathematical preparation and general programming before beginning graduate study, while its FAQ specifically requires multivariable calculus before applying and permits general programming after admission or during the MS. Additional statistics, economics and programming are preferred, and work experience is not required. The degree develops quantitative decision, strategy and organizational leadership skills; 45 units can be spread over about three to four quarters.

For Autumn 2027 MS&E MS and PhD, the current directory gives December 1, 2026 deadline and GRE General required with Mathematics Subject optional; the MS page specifies 11:59 pm PST. The department FAQ requires online application, at most two-page single-spaced purpose statement, resume, uploaded unofficial transcripts, recommendation letters and required test scores. New external applicants should include at least one academic recommender. Late applications are refused; MS decisions usually come in mid-March and PhD in mid-February via the application status page. Official scores received after deadline can still be attached if unofficial scores were entered on time, but review after two weeks is not guaranteed.

MS&E PhD students without external funding are guaranteed course assistantship support while making satisfactory progress; first-year doctoral students typically receive fellowships, and later fellowship/RA possibilities exist. MS funding is not guaranteed: students may apply for quarter-by-quarter course or research assistantships, generally confirmed at quarter start. The department says fewer than 10% of its over-200 MS students receive these appointments, mainly returning students. MS applicants should prepare to self-fund if no appointment is awarded; US federal loans are limited to US citizens/permanent residents.

ICME accepts MS and PhD applications for autumn entry through separate selections in Stanford Graduate Admissions; applicants can choose only one of the two in a given year and an unsuccessful PhD application is not reconsidered for MS. Upload unofficial transcripts for institutions attended for at least a full-time year, CV/resume, three recommendations (at least one academic strongly recommended), statements, and the required program supplement. The supplement asks for advanced course preparation with three mathematics classes required for consideration, professional/research experience and a short lay explanation of goals; PhD applicants identify nonbinding research/faculty interests, MS applicants select a track and explain career goals. GRE scores are not accepted or considered. Official transcripts are required after admission acceptance.

The 2027-28 directory lists ICME MS full-time and HCP autumn entry with January 29, 2027 deadline; PhD autumn entry is due December 1, 2026. HCP is only for MS, selected within the application, and is considered in the same pool as full-time MS. Full-time MS is designed for two years and cannot be completed wholly online; MS-to-PhD transition requires a new application. ICME says all PhD students in good standing receive departmental-standard funding through a combination of fellowship, RA and TA; MS funding is not guaranteed.

MS Design requires a science/engineering BS or equivalent and at least one year of professional employment at application submission. A BS-equivalent degree requires a supporting letter from a faculty adviser or department representative of the awarding institution. No specific design employment is required, but applicants must demonstrate a usable skill toolkit and design potential through a required digital portfolio URL. The Autumn 2027 application is due December 1, 2026 at 11:59 pm Pacific Time with a two-page maximum purpose statement, three recommendations, unofficial transcripts, applicable English results and portfolio; GRE is not required/considered. Decisions are sent by end of March 2027.

MS Design is a full-time six-quarter, two-academic-year project-based degree, with core design courses, methods/domain focus, and a year-long capstone. It is not in session during summer. The program uses Stanford Graduate Engineering 8-10 unit tuition rate; this page does not itself publish a 2027-28 amount. MS Design students are offered course assistantships upon acceptance to offset attendance cost, but offer terms vary each year. Knight-Hennessy is a separate application with October 6, 2026 1 pm Pacific deadline for the 2027 cohort.

Bioengineering MS and PhD accept applicants with an eligible bachelor's degree or equivalent without a department minimum GPA, prescribed undergraduate field or prior graduate degree. GRE is not considered. Applicants submit the online form, uploaded unofficial academic records including transcript legends, a statement of purpose of at most three single-spaced pages (two recommended), three recommendations, resume/CV and applicable English result. Official transcripts are requested only after admission is accepted; late materials may not be reviewed.

The live Graduate Admissions directory lists both Bioengineering MS and PhD for Autumn 2027-28 with December 1, 2026 deadline and GRE General/Subject not considered. Department review is holistic; virtual interviews are by invitation. BioE timeline says PhD decisions usually arrive by early March, MS decisions by early April, and admitted applicants start in September. Deferral requests are considered individually for no more than one year, generally for military, medical, visa or education reasons; this statement was posted with the older Fall 2026 cycle and must be rechecked for a 2027 offer.

The Bioengineering MS combines core quantitative biology/systems courses, technical electives, seminars and unrestricted electives with an individually planned focus and faculty adviser. It is expected to take about one year and has no thesis requirement. Named areas such as biomedical computation and imaging are examples of focus, not separate admission targets.

Bioengineering PhD research and coursework generally take five to six years; first-year students can rotate through three labs before selecting an adviser, and teaching assistant service for two courses is required. Competitive preparation includes strong quantitative mathematics/physical science and biology from coursework or research, but the department states no fixed pre-application course list. Engineering/Medicine fellowships are considered with the PhD application; Stanford Graduate Fellowship requires nomination and can provide a quarterly stipend plus 8-10 unit tuition for 12 quarters. Training-grant availability varies annually and PhD aid notifications are sent in March/April. These are selective opportunities, not guaranteed individual awards.

Chemical Engineering MS is offered externally only through the part-time Honors Cooperative Program, not as a full-time MS. HCP accepts spring and autumn entry; current 2027-28 directory and department page list January 8, 2027 for spring and April 2, 2027 for autumn. The HCP application needs an online form, two-page purpose statement, three recommendations, education/test information and uploaded unofficial transcripts; Interfolio is excluded. GRE is not accepted. Related non-ChemE majors may apply but may need extra background study after admission. The department says it cannot offer financial aid to MS students, and Knight-Hennessy does not cover this part-time route. Decisions follow within about a month after the application deadline.

Chemical Engineering PhD accepts bachelor-level entrants for Autumn 2027; prior MS and fixed undergraduate major are not required. The December 1, 2026 11:59 pm PST deadline applies to all components including three references. Submit the online application, uploaded unofficial transcripts, purpose statement up to two single-spaced pages, one-page research-experience list in the portal Resume/CV field, recommendations and applicable English scores. GRE is neither required nor accepted. Applicants from varied STEM fields are eligible; the committee values quantitative mathematics/physical-science preparation, biology and relevant ChemE concepts. Faculty do not directly admit applicants to their labs; applications cannot be updated after submission and late recommendations are not reviewed. Decisions usually arrive January/February.

Chemical Engineering PhD students in good standing are funded through thesis submission at least to the School of Engineering standard of 20-hour RA salary, tuition for required registration and Cardinal Care health insurance. Support can be fellowship, RA, training grant or TA and is arranged by the department/adviser; the student cannot be required to self-fund or obtain an external fellowship to enter or continue. The exact individual funding mix can vary by quarter.

Materials Science and Engineering accepts autumn MS and PhD applications through Stanford Graduate Admissions. For 2027 entry, PhD is due December 1, 2026 and MS January 12, 2027; GRE General/Subject are not accepted. Required materials include online application, unofficial transcripts/record legends, CV, purpose statement of no more than three single-spaced pages (two recommended), three signed institutional-letterhead recommendations with contact details, and applicable English test results. Official transcripts are required after accepted offer. PhD decisions usually arrive by late January, MS by early March; admitted students must reply by April 15, 2027. Deferrals up to one year are case-specific, usually military, medical, visa or education-related.

MSE welcomes MS/PhD applicants from engineering, related science and mathematics degrees; a prior materials major is not required. External applicants cannot apply directly to the MSE Engineer degree, which admits internal candidates only. The MS is intended as terminal study; applicants seeking both MS and PhD should apply for PhD, and may request MS consideration in the application if PhD admission is not offered.

MSE guarantees PhD students in satisfactory degree progress tuition, living stipend/salary and health insurance subsidy for the program duration; external fellowship support is topped up to department standard if insufficient. The department financial-aid page says MS students do not receive fellowships and are rarely RAs, while its FAQ says a limited number of MS fellowships may be awarded after competitive merit review. Treat MS fellowship availability as an official-source conflict, with no guaranteed award; ask MSE admissions which statement governs the 2027 cohort.

Mechanical Engineering MS applicants need a BS in engineering, physics or comparable science; an applicant who has completed or entered a Mechanical Engineering or closely related master's program, or equivalent international degree, is ineligible for the external MSME. The application requires online form, fee, two-page single-spaced purpose statement, MS supplementary responses, CV, three letters (at least one academic, two preferred), unofficial transcripts for institutions attended for at least a year, and applicable English test. GRE is not accepted through January 2027. The Autumn 2027 full-time application is due December 1, 2026; HCP has separate winter/spring windows in the live directory.

Mechanical Engineering PhD applicants need a BS in engineering, physics or comparable science and apply via Stanford Graduate Admissions with online form, fee, two-page single-spaced purpose statement, PhD supplement (research/faculty interests and short prompts), CV, three letters (at least one academic), unofficial transcripts and applicable English results. GRE is not accepted through January 2027. Autumn 2027 entry is due December 1, 2026. The department also lists winter 2026-27 and spring 2026-27 deadlines, but applicants must contact mechanical@stanford.edu before starting or submitting those off-cycle applications.

Mechanical Engineering MS is coursework-based with no thesis required; the department offers research credit by faculty arrangement. The PhD is research-intensive. ME selectively awards entering graduate fellowships, typically to PhD students; School/department awards commonly provide 8-10 units of tuition and a quarterly stipend for three to five quarters. RAs typically cover 8-10 units and salary for 20 weekly research hours, while TAs/CAs are mainly for continuing students and a limited number of entrants. These are potential funding arrangements, not an unconditional MS award or a fixed multi-year offer.

Mechanical Engineering Engineer degree requires a master's-level foundation, an additional year of study and research thesis. Admission is not granted until a faculty member agrees to supervise the thesis; external master's holders can apply if sufficiently qualified and have arranged thesis supervision and financial aid. Stanford MS students usually arrange continuation during their MS. The degree needs 90 total units, including up to 18 thesis units and at least 21 advanced technical units beyond the MS; a 3.0 GPA in non-thesis work beyond MS is required. Current Graduate Admissions directory does not list ME Engineer as an open 2027 entry; external applicants must confirm application window with ME student services rather than assume the MS/PhD deadline.

Winter 2027 applications open September 15, 2026 and close October 15; Spring 2027 December 15 to January 14, 2027; Autumn 2027 March 15 to April 20. Letters are due at the application deadline; committee decisions take about one month.

ME coterm expects differential-equations mathematics, programming and advanced engineering; unrelated majors should take at least two 100-level ME core/concentration courses. Typical A-average performance is expected, not a published numerical minimum. Submit transcript, SOP up to two single-spaced pages, CV, two Stanford-professor letters (up to three), areas of interest, short statements and preliminary proposal without adviser signature. GRE is not accepted through March 2027. Decisions take 4-6 weeks; accepted students supply adviser-signed new proposal by third week of first coterm quarter. Standard fellowships generally exclude coterms; Engineering fellowship application follows admission, RAs require faculty arrangement.

ChemE coterm needs 120 units, application by quarter before bachelor completion, unofficial Stanford/transfer transcripts, SOP maximum two single-spaced pages, two academic/professional letters and USD 125 after admission acceptance. GRE not required; no summer applications. Adviser-approved MS proposal is due by second graduate quarter or 9 graduate units, whichever first; review at 30 MS units and final approval by seventh week of preceding conferral quarter.45 MS units need letter grades where offered and GPA 3.0. Research needs adviser agreement and approved written report, and cannot replace four required 300-level core lectures.

Successful MS&E coterm candidates typically have quantitative degrees or linear algebra, multivariable calculus, programming, economics and statistics preparation. Detailed application instructions are on the current-student intranet; public directory supplies term windows, two references, optional GRE and no proposal consideration.

MS&E requires official GRE but permits hardship exemption requests; lack of quantitative degree or recent academics may make a score important competitively. Department expected English scores are old-scale TOEFL 100 or IELTS 7.5, above central minima. Tests must be taken by application deadline, not necessarily received. Three letters should be uploaded within one week; page later warns review beyond two weeks is not guaranteed. Optional paper abstract maximum two single-spaced pages.

CEE coterm application December 1, 2026 is for following Spring 2027, with no reviews May-November. Select intended CEE MS program; submit proposal, unofficial Stanford/transfer transcripts, SOP maximum three single-spaced pages (two recommended), supplement, CV and two Stanford-faculty letters. GRE not required. Late materials may not be reviewed; decisions by March 1 and response per offer. USD 125 follows accepted matriculation. CEE generally provides no coterm funding; Engineering fellowship requires admission. Eligible course transfer starts sophomore first quarter;180 bachelor plus 45 unduplicated MS units.

EE coterm does not require EE major, specific admission coursework or minimum GPA; strong engineering/physics/math preparation and high relative GPA are encouraged. No offer deferral. Submit SOP up to two single-spaced pages, exactly three letters, unofficial Stanford transcript plus transfer transcripts. EE letters are preferred; all three Stanford faculty recommended, but other references remain reviewable. USD 125 follows accepted matriculation. Coterms completing 180 units may qualify for CA/RA; funds are not guaranteed. Course transfer uses approvals from EE and home department by Final Study List deadline of final bachelor quarter, never after conferral.

MS&E HCP may be part-time on campus/remotely or full-time remotely, with limited hybrid course availability. Same degree and admission criteria; students can switch full/part-time and local/remote modes. Up to 18 NDO graduate units may count; include Stanford NDO transcript.45 units must be completed within five years. Tuition/fees go to CGOE and are slightly above Graduate Engineering rate.

value.A3i6E: The MS in Computer Science is intended as a terminal professional degree and does not lead to the PhD. Most students planning to obtain a PhD degree should apply directly for admission to the PhD program. Some students, however, may wish to complete the master’s program before deciding whether to pursue a PhD. To give such students a more significant opportunity to become familiar with research, the department has a program leading to a master’s degree with distinction in research. This program is described in more detail below.
value.WOZxr: All 45 units for the CS MS degree must be completed at Stanford.
value.ItCSB: The purpose of the master’s program is to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary for a professional career or doctoral studies. This is done through coursework in the foundational elements of the field and at least one graduate specialization. Areas of specialization include artificial intelligence, biocomputation, computer and network security, human-computer interaction, information management and analytics, real-world computing, software theory, systems, and theoretical computer science.
value.advisingExpectations: The Department of Computer Science is committed to providing academic advising in support of graduate student scholarly and professional development. When most effective, this advising relationship entails collaborative and sustained engagement by the advisor and the advisee. As a best practice, advising expectations should be periodically discussed and reviewed to ensure mutual understanding. Both the advisor and the advisee are expected to maintain professionalism and integrity. Faculty advisors guide students in critical areas such as selecting courses, designing and conducting research, developing teaching pedagogy, navigating policies and degree requirements, and exploring academic opportunities and professional pathways. Graduate students are active contributors to the advising relationship, proactively seeking academic and professional guidance and taking responsibility for informing themselves of policies and degree requirements for their graduate program. See Computer Science Graduate Advising for a statement of Computer Science policy on graduate advising. See Graduate Advising for a statement of university policy on graduate advising.
value.cotermTransferPolicy: In this master’s program, courses taken during or after the first quarter of the sophomore year are eligible for consideration for transfer to the graduate career; the timing of the first graduate quarter is not a factor. No courses taken before the first quarter of the sophomore year may be used to meet master’s degree requirements. Course transfers are not possible after the bachelor’s degree has been conferred. The university requires that the graduate advisor be assigned in the student’s first graduate quarter even though the undergraduate career may still be open. The university also requires that the Master’s Degree Program Proposal be completed by the student and approved by the department by the end of the student’s first graduate quarter.

value.source_content: The undergraduate program in Economics aims to acquaint students with the economic aspects of modern society, familiarize them with techniques for analyzing contemporary economic problems, and develop an ability to exercise judgment in evaluating public policy. The program introduces students to macro- and microeconomic theory, teaches them to think and write clearly about economic problems and policy issues and apply essential economic analysis tools. facts.value: ACT or SAT is required for first-year applicants. Stanford has no minimum score and no score guarantees admission. Either exam is accepted without preference; the redesigned ACT and original ACT are accepted, and the redesigned ACT science section is optional. Applicants self-report highest scores; official scores are required for self-reported scores if admitted and enrolling. SAT is superscored across highest Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Math sections; ACT superscore may be reported with highest section scores. Writing/essay portions are optional. Stanford recommends tests within five years.

The current Stanford page accepts both original and redesigned ACT versions and states the redesigned ACT science section is optional. Required components include Common Application; school report and counselor recommendation; official high-school transcript/academic results (grades 9–12); and two academic-teacher recommendations. School officials/testing agencies must send official records directly; applicant-submitted transcripts are not accepted. Report international curriculum results and predictions when available. Any high-school, college/university, or online courses absent from the current high-school transcript require official records.

Besides the Common App personal essay, applicants answer several Stanford short questions (each up to 50 words) and write three Stanford short essays, each 100–250 words: an idea/experience that excites learning; a note to a future roommate; and a distinctive contribution based on life experiences, interests, and character.

For 2027 entry, REA Common Application deadline is November 1, with decisions by mid-December; RD deadline is January 5, with decisions by early April. Submit by 11:59 p.m. in the applicant's local timezone. REA is nonbinding. If admitted, reply by May 1. Application with Optional Arts Portfolio uses earlier application deadlines: October 15 REA and December 5 RD.

First-year applicants who attend high school in an interview area and apply REA or RD may be invited to an optional alumni interview. Availability depends on interview-area coverage and volunteer availability; applicants cannot request or schedule one. Not receiving an interview is not a disadvantage.

Optional arts portfolios are available in Art Practice, Dance, Music, and Theater and Performance Studies for applicants wishing to show exceptional fine/performing-arts achievement. Portfolio submission does not require an arts major. Submission is through Stanford's portal after the Common Application; areas have specific materials. Music and Theater/Performance Studies may include an optional arts recommendation; none accepted for Art Practice or Dance. Mail-in items are not returned.

Undergraduate international applicants are reviewed in the context of the educational system, country, and school resources where they attend secondary school. The application process otherwise follows the same first-year or transfer route regardless of citizenship/residence. Undergraduate English-proficiency exams are not required; fluency in English is an admission prerequisite, and applicants may self-report English exam scores if they wish.

Stanford says it meets demonstrated need for admitted undergraduates regardless of citizenship when aid was requested during the application process. For international citizens, requesting aid is a factor in admission evaluation and makes the process more selective; an international citizen who applies without aid and enrolls after admission is generally ineligible to request undergraduate aid later. US citizens/permanent residents studying abroad remain domestic for aid evaluation.

Anyone who earned college credit in an associate or bachelor's degree program after high-school completion must use the transfer route. High-school/college dual-enrollment students apply as first-year. Transfer credit must be from an accredited degree-granting institution; vocational, technical, performance, or professional-program credit is excluded. Applicants need a high-school diploma/equivalent/GED to enroll. Applicants with an earned bachelor's degree are not eligible for undergraduate admission.

Stanford permits at most 90 quarter units of transfer credit (approximately two full-time years). Transfer entrants must complete at least two years of full-time enrollment at Stanford to earn a bachelor's degree, regardless of prior coursework.

facts.value: MSx is a 12-month full-time in-person Stanford GSB MS in Management. Applicants require a U.S. bachelor’s degree or equivalent (international three-year degrees included); only rare exceptions are considered. At least eight years of post-graduate professional work experience is required; managerial experience is valued but not required. No minimum GPA; application requires education history/transcripts, test score, professional history/resume (maximum two pages), two recommendations, essays and fee. GMAT, GRE or Executive Assessment is required before application with no test waivers; LSAT/MCAT are not substitutes. TOEFL/PTE/IELTS is required if English was not the primary language of instruction or any classes used another language; online PTE not accepted. Applicants report only one testing session if repeated; online GMAT/GRE/EA/TOEFL/IELTS accepted. 2026-27 rounds: Oct 8 2026, Jan 6 2027 (MBA/MSx joint), and Feb 11 2027, all 4 p.m. Pacific; decisions Dec 9 2026 or Apr 1 2027. Nonrefundable fee USD 275. A 12-month 2026-27 cost estimate is USD 221,190 single / USD 258,342 married, including tuition USD 154,828. Need-based fellowships and loans are available to admitted students regardless of citizenship; admissions decisions precede aid application.

Four LLM specializations: Corporate Governance & Practice, Environmental Law & Policy, International Economic Law, Business and Policy, and Law, Science & Technology; primary law degree must be earned outside U.S. SPILS is a research-oriented route for foreign-law-degree holders; the JSM is awarded through SPILS and requires JD/equivalent plus participation. LLM and SPILS have separate admissions decisions. JSD applicants have two routes: Stanford SPILS graduates and students from Stanford/other U.S. law schools who complete an LLM before JSD; LLM-route applicants submit serious independent original research. Neither SPILS nor Stanford LLM admission guarantees JSD. MLS is a nonprofessional degree for a small number of advanced graduate students/scholars without legal training; Bulletin inventory confirms it is not coterm.

LLM/SPILS Fall 2027 applications open Sep 15, 2026 and are due Dec 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PT; KHS file-complete deadline is same date. JSD application opens Feb 2027 and deadline is Apr 2027, both officially TBA. Advanced app fee USD 85 per program; separate fee for each program. Shared LSAC application materials: 1-2 page resume, 2-3 page personal statement, two recommendation letters, official transcripts, TOEFL; SPILS/JSD add research proposal and third letter; JSD also requires 1-2 examples of English scholarly writing. LSAC CAS and recommendation service required; direct submissions rejected. TOEFL iBT minimum is 100 before Jan 21, 2026; for tests on/after that date, overall 5.5 with reading/listening at least 5.5 and writing/speaking at least 5.0. Scores to LSAC institution code 8395. Native-English applicants still request TOEFL waiver; full-time study/work in English for at least two years may qualify with formal request/evidence. LLM normally expects two years legal practice; waiver explanation possible. Decisions expected by mid-April 2027.

The 12-month MSx program cost of attendance for July 2026-June 2027 is USD 221,190 for a single student and USD 258,342 for a married student; tuition is USD 154,828. Budget includes housing, living expenses, USD 250 documentation fee, medical insurance, health fee. Eligible child allowances are separately estimated. Need-based gap between attendance cost and expected student contribution is covered by a mix of fellowship and loans; fellowship is gift aid, based solely on demonstrated need, and is available regardless of citizenship.

Stanford Law says it provides no scholarship or stipend funding to LLM students. SPILS funding exists only to an extremely limited degree. Admitted JSD students may receive some need-based aid and research/conference funding; no coverage amount or renewal terms are published. KHS is separately applied for; up to three years of funding may be available, with separate timing and eligibility. MLS program funding was not stated on reviewed official pages.

Stanford's official 2026-27 Law School tuition category is USD 26,593 per quarter; the published rate is by Law School classification and not limited to JD. LLM programs are nine months/three quarters, so the listed tuition rate establishes the applicable quarterly rate, while the standard single-student cost-of-attendance page separately estimates USD 125,124 on-campus or USD 126,216 off-campus. The COA page does not identify which advanced degree cases its living/loan budget covers. MLS requires at least three residency quarters and full Law School tuition; program-specific non-tuition fees or special registration changes should be confirmed.

JD requires 111 units over no less than three academic years. LLM requires 35-45 approved quarter units, three quarters in residence, at least 26 Law units and full tuition; residence is at least 9 enrolled units and 8 passed units each quarter, with work limited to 20 hours weekly; LLM is a full nine-month academic year. JSM requires 35 units, with thesis and public presentation, and is expected to finish in one academic year (two consecutive years maximum). MLS requires 37 units, three residency quarters, and is expected to finish in one academic year (two consecutive years maximum). JSD requires 44 residency units, including one academic year in residence, and independent dissertation research; award duration beyond minimum residency is not specified.

Stanford Law advanced applicants must submit TOEFL iBT (not IELTS under the current Law advanced process). Minimum: 100 for tests before Jan 21, 2026; for tests on/after, overall 5.5 with reading/listening >=5.5 and writing/speaking >=5.0. facts.value: Applicants must hold, or expect before enrollment to hold, a U.S. bachelor’s degree or international equivalent from a recognized institution. WES evaluation is not required with application; admitted international-degree holders may be asked for WES verification after accepting an offer.

For 2027-28 entry, absent an exemption, official TOEFL iBT or IELTS Academic required: minimum consideration TOEFL 90 (before 2026-01-21), TOEFL 4.5 (on/after), or IELTS 7; programs may set higher thresholds. Valid two years; earliest date Sep. 1, 2024.

Each program separately marks GRE General/Subject required, optional, or not considered. Required scores sent officially; self-reported scores suffice initially. Valid five years; earliest date for 2027-28 entry Sep. 1, 2021.

Central application gathers background, academic history/transcripts, applicable tests, experience, three academic/professional references, statement of purpose, program supplement and additional information. Programs may add essays, writing samples, portfolio, audition, CV or other items.
One application per academic year for one nonprofessional graduate degree program.
2027-28 application is open. Each program sets its own deadline. Submit materials by that deadline and finalize/pay by 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.
USD 125, nonrefundable; pay on submission by credit card or U.S. checking-account bank transfer.
Before submitting, applicants may request GRE fee reduction, eligible-program participation, or school-based waiver. Submit at least 10 business days before program deadline for timely decision.
Graduate study generally requires full-time enrollment (at least 8 units per academic quarter) and significant campus presence, unless the degree program approves reduced/minimal presence.

University minimum for most master’s programs: 45 Stanford units, all 100-level or above, with at least 50% primarily for graduate students (typically 200-level+). Coterminal candidates have three years from first graduate quarter. Program requirements may exceed these minima.

External MS deadline January 15, 2027 for Autumn 2027–28. Requires online application and fee, statement of purpose, three recommendations, official transcripts and English test where applicable. GRE General is optional; original research paper is encouraged but not required. The research-based MS requires a thesis; external students normally need 4–6 quarters. Program provides no regular financial aid; RA/TA positions may be available by quarter, but are not assured for the full degree. Decisions mid- to late-March.

Current coterm directory lists Spring 2026–27 deadline January 15, 2027 and Autumn 2027–28 deadline May 3, 2027. GRE General is optional; two recommendations and a program proposal are required. This current-student route has distinct requirements from the external route, which requires three recommendations.
